newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police hold fire in jail riots.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police hold fire in jail riots.

text.p: Bangladesh on Friday strengthened security at prisons nationwide to prevent further unrest as rebellious prisoners refused to give up sieges at two jails.
Extra police and paramilitary troops were positioned inside and around penal compounds across the country, police said.
A revolt at Jessore Jail in western Bangladesh entered its fifth day on Friday, prompted by anger over a limited Independence Day amnesty for prisoners.
The uprising began on Monday when prisoners armed with knives and iron bars chased away guards and took control. About 2,000 police and troops have since surrounded the jail.
On Thursday, prisoners in northwestern Tangail Jail, prompted by the Jessore revolt, rebelled, taking five jail officials hostage.
A third revolt in southern Barisal Jail was quickly suppressed on Thursday by guards after fighting lasting about an hour.
A similar revolt in Dhaka's central jail was broken up almost as soon as it started on Friday.
The trouble started after 90 prisoners were freed under an amnesty marking the country's 25th independence anniversary on Monday.
Angered at being left out, prisoners at Jessore launched their riot, with some demanding freedom and others seeking better treatment and food, police said. The revolt had a knock-on effect.
"All efforts to peacefully end the jail crises have apparently failed after the prisoners refused to give up. We have not yet decided whether to use force to end the crisis," said one police officer.
A government official said some prisoners were demanding to see Home Minister Rafiqul Islam to air their grievances and that police had been told to try to avoid using force at all costs.
The minister was not available for comment.
